# YM46: 文源阁 Wenyuan Ge, "The Wen Yuan Ko, Library of the Source of Literature"

Wave 1 · Yuanming Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=YM46` · Page: `/scenes/#YM46` · Row: `research/buildings/YM46-wenyuan-ge/`

## What it was

文源阁 Wenyuan Ge, the library that held a set of the 四库全书, stands a little west of north of 水木明瑟, with 柳浪闻莺 to the west (S05 j81:35b-36a, E2195). S05 dates it 乾隆三十九年 (1774) and pairs it with 文渊阁 in the palace and 文津阁 at Chengde (j81:36a). Qianlong's 文源阁记, cut on a stele in a pavilion east of the library, says he took the form of 天一阁, the Fan family library in Zhejiang, whose bay count and beam and column sizes follow the idea 'heaven one gives birth to water' (天一生水) (j81:36b-37a, E2194). It has six bays on each of two floors (j81:35b); the 2024 dig confirms six bays and black glazed roof tiles (E2207, S133). The pierced rock 玲峰 from 大房山 stands in the pool in front (j81:36b-39a). Malone saw the stele still standing and fragments of white-and-green wave-pattern glazed tile (S02 pp.89-90, E2198). The library and its books burned in October 1860 with the garden (E0485).

From the inventory row: **built** 乾隆三十九年 1774 [j81:36a]; 1775; **changed** Layout unchanged from the conversion of 1775 to the end: the dig matches Yangshi Lei sketches dated 1779 and 1898; **destroyed** 1860; library burnt (S02 p.188); stele and rock survived the fire (S02 p.89) (S05, S02, S45, S01, S337, S361, S942).

## The scene itself

### The leaf of 1744, its poem and preface

Not one of the Forty Scenes (built 1774). The texts that stand for the leaf are Qianlong's 文源阁记 and poems in S05 j81:36b-39a: '因輯四庫全書命取其閣式以構庋貯之' ('compiling the Four Treasuries, I ordered its pavilion form taken to build a store for them', E2194); the 1776 poem '天一取閣式 文津實先構' (E2186); and two songs of 1775-76 on the 玲峰 rock, said to surpass the 'eighty-one holes' of Mi Fu's famous stone (E2181, E2185). The library replaced the Yongzheng pavilion 四达亭 (params.json, S134).

### How later sources differ

The only plan of 文源阁 found on mhymy is Tsinghua T0049, dated 光绪二十四年 (1898), a presentation sheet of 1225x700 mm: 38 years after the burning, so a survey or project on the ruin, not the 1860 state (S310 rec. 7842; E2205). The record dates the library to 乾隆四十年 (1775), built on the site of the square double-eaved 四达亭 of 1731, whose inner screens Castiglione painted in 1728. The NLC 文源阁图样 (E2204) remains undated beyond 清末.

### The garden around it

A rock garden round a pool: the monolith 玲峰, 'with inscriptions on it and pierced with many holes, rising 12 or 15 feet from a stone terrace in the middle of the pool' (S02 pp.89-90, E2198), with Qianlong's poem cut on it (S05 j81:36b). The 1776 poem speaks of a 月台 and 'strange stones heaped into peaks' (詭石堆竒岫, j81:37b). The dig found two ponds, one before and one east of the library, walls of 虎皮石 rubble, and the base of 玲峰 of long slabs tied with iron dovetails (E2206, E2207).

## What survives today

Before the 2024 dig the library and stele-pavilion platforms were fairly whole, with the gate, steps, a cracked-ice floor and black and green glazed scraps on the ground; the square pond had gone and the 玲峰 rock lay broken in two (S105 sect. 3.2). The 2024 dig (August to November, 北京市考古研究院) found the gate, the north gate, library and stele-pavilion foundations, walls of rubble, flagstone paths, the 玲峰 base, two ponds and five culverts, and confirmed six bays and black glazed tiles (S133; S134; S942). Sizes in metres from the dig are not yet published; the Guangxu 丈尺册 gives the bays (S105 note [4]).

## The best views for modellers

No pre-1860 Yangshi Lei plan of 文源阁 was found on mhymy; the Tsinghua plan T0049 is of 1898. The river-and-revetment plan 样043-1 (E0540) shows the 文源阁 court of 1775 at about 1:200 and is the best period plan for its footprint.
